Suez Canal Disruption Escalates as Political Unrest Grips Egypt, Global Trade Impacted

Cairo—Widespread political unrest in Egypt has severely disrupted transit through the Suez Canal, with the Egyptian Navy imposing new restrictions as protests and clashes continue in major cities. The unrest, now entering its second week, follows the government’s announcement of emergency austerity measures and a controversial restructuring of fuel subsidies.

Traffic through the vital waterway, which handles roughly 12% of global trade, has slowed to less than half its normal volume since Friday, according to data from the International Shipping Council. Several vessels, including oil tankers and container ships, remain anchored off Port Said and Suez, awaiting clearance as authorities conduct enhanced security checks.

The Egyptian Ministry of Transport stated Monday, “We are committed to ensuring the safety of all ships and crew while maintaining operations in the Canal as circumstances permit.” However, on-the-ground reports from the Egyptian Dockworkers Union describe mounting logistical challenges, with thousands of workers unable to reach port facilities due to road blockades and curfews imposed in Cairo, Alexandria, and Ismailia.

Global markets reacted sharply, with crude oil prices rising 4% in early trading and the cost of container freight between Asia and Europe up 11% week-on-week, according to the Global Maritime Index. “The Suez is a chokepoint for world trade,” said Lina Haddad, lead analyst at Nexus Commodities. “Prolonged disruption could ripple through supply chains and inflation forecasts.”

While Egyptian authorities have pledged to restore order, business leaders and international observers warn that ongoing instability could further strain Egypt’s fragile economy and disrupt critical supply routes for weeks to come.
